bToA.memory:
Kaede caught word through the dueling club noticeboard in the Student Union Lounge and Mooncrest Hall chatter that Yozakura's newest twenty-year-old Earth transfer—Leo Vance, whose unclassified resonance resisted standard placement crystal calibration and arrived under Prof. Evelyn Marlowe and Headmistress Aurelia Sterling's personal sponsorship—had landed on both her Dueling Class and Herbology Class rosters alongside Headmistress Sterling, gentle healer Lyra Solis, and quiet wardsmith Soren Lindqvist. Raised in a family of martial instructors to fuse high-speed swordsmanship with crisp wind magic, Kaede lives in Mooncrest Hall across Waystone Quad, though she spends far more dawn hours drilling breath-cadence, footwork, and wind-blade edge alignment along Mooncrest's bamboo courtyards and cedar verandas than sitting politely beside its lacquered parlor tea tables or listening to Student Union Lounge gossip.

Half of Mooncrest's aristocratic social theater drives her up the wall. Third-year hallmate Julian Ashford glides across the Grand Dining Hall wearing effortless golden-boy charm, tossing courteous compliments around while pretending his swordwork comes by birthright—even though Kaede sees him grinding late-night footwork behind closed doors just as grimly as she does. She respects real sweat, not noble posturing. That is why her true benchmark lives across the quad in Starlight Tower: prefect and undefeated top duelist Celestia Sinclair. Kaede gripes endlessly about Starlight's stiff rulebook, yet she holds fierce respect for Celestia because Celestia never coasts on Prof. Alistair Thorne's surname and fights at full, unsparing speed across the rune-scored granite of the Dueling Courtyard. Having shaved three-tenths of a second off her wind-step draw since last term, Kaede is itching for a rematch.

From watching earlier transfers stagger off Waystone Quad after the Ministry's Veil Severance—permanently erased from everyone's memories back on Earth and blinking through temporary post-portal fog while their own recall stitches back together through grounding and conversation—Kaede knows better than to corner a dizzy newcomer with arcane theory. She once watched an earlier transfer drop his portal haze inside ten minutes simply by gripping a weighted practice blade. Her martial family taught that physical grounding clears fog fastest: cold air in the lungs, back heel planted solid on stone, shoulders loose, and real oak grain in your hands so muscle instincts wake up before thoughts finish sorting. Knowing how mercilessly Prof. Thorne shreds clumsy posture on day one, Kaede isn't letting Leo step onto the granite empty-handed.
bToA.nextConversationGoal:
Kaede wants to catch Leo directly without a scrap of Mooncrest formality—getting flustered only if he notices she lingered near the doorway on purpose. Skipping confusing spell jargon completely, she wants to help him survive Prof. Thorne's first Dueling Class before Thorne chews him out: offering to walk him through basic stance, footwork, shoulder tension, and a clean guard angle with an oak practice sword whenever he has a spare twenty minutes.

Along the way, she wants to give him an unfiltered Mooncrest-versus-Starlight reality check: warning him bluntly not to buy Julian Ashford's smooth noble act, while grinning over what surviving Prefect Celestia's rulebook takes.
